Subject: Acme / Redwood — post-demo recap & procurement path

Hi Sofia / Tom —

Great to meet earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so nothing gets lost: 

1) What we agreed: Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU capacity) to host the GenAssist model for your support summarization use case.
2) Primary constraints you mentioned: 1) Procurement prefers PO payment and standard enterprise T&Cs, 2) Security team will run a short questionnaire (SOC2 + data handling), and 3) you’d like to explore if a marketplace purchase (AWS/GCP Marketplace) is an easier path for billing.

Next steps (proposed):
- I will share the standard pricing sheet and our enterprise terms for legal (attached).
- You will confirm whether procurement needs a SOW or if a master services agreement + PO is sufficient.
- Rishi will follow up on any discount/term questions and provide a draft mutual action plan if you’d like.

If helpful I can set a weekly 15-min check-in (Fri mornings) to keep momentum.

Attachments: redwood-pricing-sheet-STD-2026.pdf, redwood-saas-terms-2026.pdf

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap. A couple quick clarifications from procurement: 
- We generally prefer PO billing for multi-month contracts (our AP team issues POs monthly or quarterly).
- Legal will likely request a short redline to the attached terms; can you confirm which clauses are negotiable (primarily liability/indemnity, data residency)?
- Marketplace is interesting because it’d simplify billing, but we'd need to confirm feature parity and whether marketplace billing incurs different SLAs/pricing.

We’d also appreciate any standard SOC2 evidence + an answers doc to our procurement questionnaire. I attached the initial questionnaire (acme-procurement-questions.xlsx).

I’m going to loop in our procurement lead if we proceed.

Best,

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>; Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 30 Oct 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme / Redwood — procurement clarifications + evidence

Tom / Sofia —

Thanks — appreciate the details. Quick replies below: 

- PO vs Card: We support both. For Reserved Dedicated seats we typically set up a yearly commitment invoiced net-30 by PO, but we can do monthly invoices as well if that helps. If you prefer Marketplace, pricing is functionally equivalent but billing flows through the marketplace vendor which can add ~45-60 days for provisioning and sometimes changes contract language. I can put together a side-by-side.

- Negotiable terms: We are open to discussing liability and indemnity within reason; we typically have carve-outs for third-party model liabilities and standard caps tied to fees. I’ll ask legal to highlight negotiable sections in the attached terms.

- SOC2 + evidence: Dev is copying in our compliance lead; we'll provide SOC2 report excerpt and an answers doc for the questionnaire. Expect files early next week.

Proposed next step: I’ll schedule a 15-min touchpoint next Friday (Nov 6) to review outstanding items unless you prefer to accelerate. Also looping Rishi for commercial cadence/discount guidance.

Thanks,
Marissa

---
Attachments incoming: redwood-soc2-summary.pdf (will follow), answers to acme-procurement-questions.xlsx

Hi Tom / Sofia —

Quick note from a commercial standpoint: 
- If Acme is willing to commit to a 12-month reserved capacity, we can offer a tiered discount (details in attached pricing sheet).
- If you need the Marketplace route for procurement reasons, we can dedicate spot capacity to mirror the Dedicated plan but Marketplace orders typically can’t be retroactively credited for committed discounts, so plan accordingly.

Marissa and I can work with your AP/procurement lead on PO terms. If you share the name of the procurement contact, we’ll send a short MPO (master purchase order) template to expedite processing.

Regards,
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Sales, Enterprise | Redwood Inference
